title: Ukraine Support Act
official_title: To authorize support for Ukraine, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: The sponsor is a Democrat in the Republican-majority House and the bill carries 43 cosponsors. Its expanded Russia sanctions, 500 percent tariffs, and additional Ukraine funding face uncertain support in the Senate, where 60 votes would be required, and the broad presidential waiver and termination authority over the sanctions may further shape its path.
summary: This bill expands U.S. support for Ukraine through diplomacy, military assistance, and a broad sanctions regime against Russia. It extends Lend-Lease and loan authority, creates a Ukraine Reconstruction Trust Fund, and requires the President to impose sanctions, 500 percent tariffs, and a 100 percent tax on blocked Russian and Belarusian sovereign-asset income once Russia is found to be waging war or refusing peace.
brief: Expands U.S. security assistance for Ukraine and requires mandatory sanctions, tariffs, and asset taxes against Russia upon a presidential determination.

top_lines.headline: Security Assistance for Ukraine
subs: Extends Ukraine Lend-Lease authority through fiscal year 2028
Raises the Ukraine and NATO direct-loan ceiling to $8B
Adds $300M for the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative in 2026 and 2027

top_lines.headline: Sanctions and Tariffs on Russia
subs: President must decide every 90 days whether Russia is waging war or refusing peace
Triggers mandatory sanctions on 13 named Russian banks and oil, gas, and mining firms
Raises duties on all Russian imports to at least 500 percent

top_lines.headline: Reconstruction and Diplomacy
subs: Creates a Ukraine Reconstruction Trust Fund in the Treasury
100 percent tax on blocked Russian and Belarusian sovereign-asset income
Authorizes $250M for Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty for 2026

sections.label: Title I - Diplomacy and Support for Ukraine

items.main: Establishes a Ukraine Reconstruction Trust Fund in the Treasury for rebuilding, humanitarian aid, economic growth, and governance in Ukraine.
items.detail: Added as Section 9512 of the Internal Revenue Code, the fund receives revenues from the tax imposed under new section 892A and is available to the Secretary of State subject to Foreign Assistance Act requirements. The bill also creates an Insurance for Ukraine Initiative in the State Department and codifies a Special Coordinator for Ukrainian Reconstruction.

items.main: Authorizes $250M for Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty for fiscal year 2026 and $30M for each of fiscal years 2025 through 2029 for U.S.-European nuclear energy cooperation.
items.detail: It directs a strategy to counter Russian influence in Europe's nuclear energy sector and extends federal war-risk insurance eligibility for vessels trading with Ukraine for 5 years. It also directs use of the Countering Russian Influence Fund to help Ukraine combat disinformation.

items.main: Extends Ukraine Lend-Lease authority through fiscal year 2028 and raises the direct-loan ceiling for Ukraine and NATO allies to $8B.
items.detail: Amends the Ukraine Democracy Defense Lend-Lease Act of 2022 from fiscal years 2022 and 2023 to fiscal years 2022 through 2028. Through fiscal year 2026, direct loans under Section 23 of the Arms Export Control Act may be made available with gross obligations not to exceed $8B, raised from $4B, and adds recovery-and-return reporting.

items.main: Extends the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative with $300M for fiscal year 2026 and $300M for fiscal year 2027, and authorizes support for Baltic countries.
items.detail: Amends Section 1250 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2016, extending its authority from December 31, 2026 to December 31, 2027. It authorizes $30M in Foreign Military Financing grants and $4M in nonproliferation and anti-terrorism programs per Baltic country for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2028.

sections.label: Title III - Sanctions and Export Controls

items.main: Requires the President to determine within 15 days, and at least every 90 days, whether Russia is waging a war of aggression or refusing to negotiate or honor a peace agreement, triggering mandatory sanctions.
items.detail: Upon an affirmative determination, the President must within 15 days sanction 3 or more of 13 named financial institutions, including the Central Bank of the Russian Federation, and all Russian oil, gas, coal, and mineral companies, and specified Russian officials.

items.main: Raises duties on all Russian imports to at least 500 percent, bans energy products refined from Russian crude, and imposes a 100 percent tax on blocked Russian and Belarusian sovereign-asset income.
items.detail: The 500 percent ad valorem duty and import ban apply after an affirmative determination. The 100 percent tax falls on interest and dividends from Russian and Belarusian assets blocked under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act and applies without regard to any U.S. treaty obligation.

items.main: Sets a congressional review process for lifting Russia sanctions and a termination-and-reimposition mechanism.
items.detail: The President may terminate sanctions, duties, and export controls on certifying that Russia has ceased its war or peace-agreement violations, and must immediately reimpose them if Russia restarts. The President may also waive individual sanctions on determining a waiver is vital to national security, with 15 days' notice to Congress.

underreported.summary: Applies the 100 percent tax on blocked Russian and Belarusian sovereign-asset income without regard to any U.S. treaty obligation.
underreported.why_unreported: This overrides existing U.S. tax-treaty obligations, an effect beyond the sanctions and support purposes stated in the bill's titles.

underreported.summary: Lets the President waive any Title III sanction on determining the waiver is vital to national security, with 15 days' notice to Congress.
underreported.why_unreported: The sanctions are described as mandatory upon a determination, but this provision preserves broad presidential discretion to waive them case by case.

underreported.summary: Deems NATO-, Ukraine-, or designated-country-owned vessels trading with Ukraine eligible for federal war-risk insurance for 5 years.
underreported.why_unreported: This extends federal war-risk insurance exposure to foreign-owned commercial vessels, a financial commitment not apparent from the bill's support framing.

gaps: The bill establishes a Ukraine Reconstruction Trust Fund funded by a tax on blocked sovereign-asset income but does not estimate how much revenue that tax will raise.
The bill authorizes appropriations for Radio Free Europe, nuclear cooperation, and Baltic support but does not itself appropriate those funds.

The bill makes sanctions mandatory upon a determination but lets the President waive any of them for national security and terminate them all on a certification, without specifying limits on that discretion.
The bill raises duties on Russian imports to at least 500 percent but, apart from the oil-refinery ban, does not address transshipment of Russian goods through third countries.
The bill raises the direct-loan ceiling for Ukraine and NATO allies to $8B but does not set repayment or recovery terms beyond those in existing law.

A sanctions-trigger regime requiring mandatory sanctions on Russian banks, energy and mining firms, and officials upon a presidential determination
A 500 percent duty on Russian imports, a ban on energy products refined from Russian crude, and a 100 percent tax on blocked Russian and Belarusian sovereign-asset income
